newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore says electronic stock services a success.
newsitem.headline: Singapore says electronic stock services a success.

text.p: The Singapore Stock Exchange (SES) has introduced some services to enhance trading services for investors which have been "remarkably successful", exchange chairman Chua Kim Yeow said on Friday.
He told a seminar on that more than 96 percent of initial public offer (IPO) share applications were made through electronic transfer last year.
The Electronic Share Application System (ESA), started in 1993, allows those with bank accounts and an automated transfer machine (ATM) card with a bank to apply for newly-listed shares.
"The applications made through ESA for some foreign currency issues reached 99 percent," he said.
Chua said that in light of the success, the SES will allow investors to make applications for rights issues through similar methods from the middle of September.
This means investors no longer have to line up for cashier orders and submit application forms.
Chua said that Direct Crediting Service (CDP) for account holders, started in 1996, was another triumph for the SES.
Cash dividends and other cash distributions by listed local companies are credited directly to a bank account designated by the CDP account holder.
Last year, 80 percent of total dividends were paid through this method, he said.
"This means 1.9 million fewer cheques were issued and processed," Chua said.

Electronic Payment for Shares (EPS), introduced at the end of last year, allows investors to transfer funds electronically from a bank to a stockbroking company to pay for shares and that, too, had bee successful, he said.
A total of Singapore $1.3 billion was electronically transferred in the first half of this year.
Chua said a new settlement scheme to improve efficiency for institutional investors -- Delivery Versus Payment (DVP) in Singapore dollars -- would begin on August 1.
Custodian banks settling for institutional investors will take on counterparty risks against direct crediting, rather than broking firms, as is the case now.
CDP will settle with all custodian banks and broking firms.
Chua said the SES would continue to ensure that initiatives and programmes were in place to ensure it is well regulated, safe, fair and competitive.
